gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AC180's add-on pack feeds the station only through its 500 W (12–60 V) solar/DC input in Power Bank Mode. Under any load above 500 W, the AC180's own 1,152 Wh battery still drains, at the load minus 500 W.
standout_why: I opened stormwatts.com (cited), batteryrank.com (cited), watthourlab.com (cited) and offgridfieldguide.com (cited). offgridfieldguide already says the AC180 has 'no dedicated battery port' and that B80/B230/B300 packs connect 'by cable through the DC input, for up to 4,224Wh'. stormwatts lists the AC180 as not expandable, and ChatGPT's third answer already says 'power-bank mode … isn't equivalent to integrated expansion'. None of them gives the 500 W ceiling on that path, the Power Bank Mode requirement, or the separate P090D cable. None says what that ceiling means at loads above 500 W. batteryrank and stormwatts only say to 'confirm the cable' for EcoFlow's extra-battery port. watthourlab and batteryrank say a pack adds Wh, not W. The core mechanism is already partly out there, so only the 500 W consequence is new.
decides: The AC180 belongs with the 'can't truly expand' models, not alongside the DELTA 3 / 3 Plus, Jackery 1000 Plus / HomePower 1000 Plus v2, DJI Power 1000 V2 and OUPES Mega 1. Its pack is an external charger capped at 500 W, not a battery on the station's internal bus, and it needs a separate P090D cable. Our page's AC180 row ('max 4,224 Wh', B300) should say this. The B300 is also sold out at $1,399 today. The pick stays a model with a dedicated extra-battery port, such as the EcoFlow DELTA 3 / 3 Plus.

findings.label: How the B80/B230/B300 connect
findings.value: Through cables, with the battery in Power Bank Mode: 'To connect B80 batteries, you'll need the Aviation to DC7909 cable' and 'the P090D cable is required for B230/B300 batteries.' 'Please make sure the batteries are in Power Bank Mode.'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station (BLUETTI Australia)
findings.note: Verbatim FAQ text on BLUETTI's own Australian page. The same FAQ says 'Currently, the AC180 supports capacity expansion with B80, B230, or B300 batteries' and that the cable was 'expected to start selling in late June'. The US page could not be opened (HTTP 429), so the US wording is unverified.

findings.label: Solar/DC input the pack feeds through
findings.value: 500 W max, open-circuit voltage 12–60 V DC, 10 A
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station (BLUETTI Australia)
findings.note: Spec line 'Solar Input: 500W Max., VOC 12-60VDC, 10A'. The page does not itself say 'DC input' next to the expansion FAQ. I linked the pack to this input because the FAQ cable ends in DC7909, which is the AC180's solar/DC input, and because offgridfieldguide.com says the packs connect 'through the DC input'. My arithmetic: at an 1,800 W load the internal battery drains at about 1,300 W (1,800 − 500), so the pack slows the drain but cannot carry the load.
